newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Gujral told to drop ex-boss from coalition.
newsitem.headline: India's Gujral told to drop ex-boss from coalition.

text.p: The left-wing allies of Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral on Tuesday urged him to kick his former party boss out of the United Front coalition.

Janata Dal's former president Laloo Prasad Yadav, who is mired in a corruption scandal, on Saturday quit his old party to lead a powerful breakaway group that has named itself the Rashtriya (Nationalist) Janata Dal.

"The left parties are of the view that Laloo's Rashtriya (Nationalist) Janata Dal should not be admitted in the United Front," Harkishen Singh Surjeet, secretary general of Communist Party of India (Marxist), told a news briefing.
Gujral also faced pressure from left-wing parties to recommend the dismissal of Yadav as chief minister of the eastern state of Bihar.
Yadav has been indicted in a $280 million corruption scandal. But he says he is innocent and has rejected calls from alliance partners to step down.
Yadav has said he would continue to support the centre-left government, in which three of his supporters are ministers.
The leftist parties asked Gujral to drop the three ministers from his council.
"The three ministers should be removed. They are a part of a faction which is out to disrupt United Front," Surjeet said.
The leftist parties will step up their political campaign against Yadav in a bid to force him to step down as state chief minister, leaders said.
"I have no intention to remove the three ministers," Gujral was earlier quoted by the Press Trust of India (PTI) as saying in an interview with a private television channel.
The Core Committee of the United Front, representing a select panel of senior leaders of the alliance, is expected to meet soon to discuss the demands of the leftist parties, political leaders said.
"Gujral has a problem on his hand. He seems to unwilling to bell the Laloo Prasad cat," political analyst Rasheed Talib said.
The Congress party, which provides crucial support to Gujral's government, may also flex its muscles with an eye to dislodging the alliance.

In addition, Gujral must look over his shoulder for any moves by the main opposition Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) to take advantage of the coalition's disarray, political analysts said.
The BJP emerged as the single largest party with 162 deputies in the 545-seat parliament after an inconclusive general election in May last year.
The Hindu nationalists have urged President Shankar Dayal Sharma to dismiss Yadav as Bihar chief minister and have launched a massive political campaign in the state.
